pages.text: Papiliontina was a genus of very large cicadas from the Middle Triassic of MaÃ©dygen, Kyrgizstan. It is probably the best-preserved and therefore best-known triassic member of the Palaeontinidae, a now-extinct diverse family of giant moth-like cicadas quite widespread and abundant during the Mesozoic period.

Papiliontina is particularly notable for the presence of large intimidating eyespots, mimicking the eyes of a large predator, on each of its forewings, a trait unique in palaeontinids. Papiliontina, like other palaeontinids, probably held its wings opened when resting, revealing a wide grinning face made to terrify its many potential predators, in the same manner than many modern owlet-moths and flower mantis.
